newsitem.title: USA: North Dakota wheat harvest advances to 63 pct.
newsitem.headline: North Dakota wheat harvest advances to 63 pct.

text.p: Hot, dry weather allowed harvesting of North Dakota's spring wheat crop to advance during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop progress report.
But the heat, dryness and grasshopper infestations hurt crops and pastures.
Sixty-three percent of the spring wheat acreage was combined versus 49 last year and the 55 average. Spring wheat was rated 61 percent good to excellent, 27 fair, 10 poor and two very poor.
Percentage condition for other grains was as follows (from good to poor): durum, 48, 34, 14 and four; corn 56, 30 and 14.
Thirty-three percent of the state's durum was combined, versus 28 last year and 38 on average. Seventy-seven percent of the barley was combined versus 65 last year and the 76 average.
Topsoil moisture was rated two percent surplus, 50 adequate, 28 short and 20 very short. Subsoil moisture was rated three percent surplus, 53 adequate, 30 short and 14 very short.
Pasture conditions decreased and were rated 39 percent good to excellent, 34 fair, 19 poor and eight very poor.
